title: Thermal runaway on edge gateway devices due to fan assembly failure
description: Multiple edge gateway devices in Building C reported sustained temperature readings above 85°C over a 15-minute period. Normal operating temperature for these devices is 45-55°C. The temperature increase was gradual (approximately 2°C per minute) rather than instantaneous, suggesting a cooling system degradation rather than an external heat source. Affected devices were co-located in a single server rack with shared cooling infrastructure.
root_cause: The rack-mounted cooling fan assembly experienced bearing failure, reducing airflow by approximately 70%. The gradual temperature rise pattern is characteristic of progressive mechanical degradation rather than sudden failure. Post-incident inspection revealed metal shavings in the fan housing consistent with bearing wear.
resolution_steps: Immediately reduce workload on affected devices to lower heat generation
Verify fan assembly RPM via firmware diagnostics interface
Replace failed fan assembly with rated replacement unit
Apply fresh thermal paste to heat sinks if temperature exceeded 90°C for more than 5 minutes
Monitor temperature readings for 24 hours post-repair to confirm resolution
Schedule preventive fan replacement for all units exceeding 18 months of operation
